chapterTitle: The Fifth and Sixth Trumpets: Locusts from the Abyss and Horsemen from the Euphrates

scripture.text: The fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star from the sky which had fallen to the earth. The key to the pit of the abyss was given to him.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν, “The fifth angel sounded” — σαλπίζω: the first ‘woe’. καὶ εἶδον ἀστέρα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεπτωκότα εἰς τὴν γῆν, “and I saw a star from the sky which had fallen to the earth” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family); γῆ, from the world family. Perfect tense: already fallen. Stars often stand for angels (1:20); a fallen star suggests a fallen angel — Jesus said, “I saw Satan having fallen like lightning from heaven” (Luke 10:18). καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἡ κλεὶς τοῦ φρέατος τῆς ἀβύσσου, “The key to the pit of the abyss was given to him” — ‘given’: even the forces of hell act only by permission. Christ holds the keys of death and Hades (1:18).

scripture.text: He opened the pit of the abyss, and smoke went up out of the pit, like the smoke from a burning furnace. The sun and the air were darkened because of the smoke from the pit.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἤνοιξεν τὸ φρέαρ τῆς ἀβύσσου, “He opened the pit of the abyss” — ἄβυσσος, the bottomless deep, the prison of demons (Luke 8:31). καὶ ἀνέβη καπνὸς ἐκ τοῦ φρέατος ὡς καπνὸς καμίνου μεγάλης, “and smoke went up out of the pit, like the smoke from a burning furnace” — like the smoke over Sodom. καὶ ἐσκοτώθη ὁ ἥλιος καὶ ὁ ἀὴρ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ τοῦ φρέατος, “The sun and the air were darkened because of the smoke from the pit” — σκοτόω, from the darkness family: to darken, to obscure. Evil from the abyss blots out the light.

scripture.text: Then out of the smoke came locusts on the earth, and power was given to them, as the scorpions of the earth have power.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ ἐξῆλθον ἀκρίδες εἰς τὴν γῆν, “Then out of the smoke came locusts on the earth” — ἀκρίς: the eighth plague of Egypt, and Joel's devastating locust army; γῆ, from the world family. καὶ ἐδόθη αὐταῖς ἐξουσία ὡς ἔχουσιν ἐξουσίαν οἱ σκορπίοι τῆς γῆς, “and power was given to them, as the scorpions of the earth have power” — ἐξουσία, from the power family, twice: delegated authority, as distinct from δύναμις, inherent ability; ‘given’ again: they act only by permission.

scripture.text: They were told that they should not hurt the grass of the earth, neither any green thing, neither any tree, but only those people who don’t have God’s seal on their foreheads.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐρρέθη αὐταῖς ἵνα μὴ ἀδικήσουσιν τὸν χόρτον τῆς γῆς, “They were told that they should not hurt the grass of the earth” — ἀδικέω; γῆ, from the world family. Ordinary locusts eat grass; these do not. οὐδὲ πᾶν χλωρὸν οὐδὲ πᾶν δένδρον, “neither any green thing, neither any tree” — εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους οἵτινες οὐκ ἔχουσι τὴν σφραγῖδα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων, “but only those people who don’t have God’s seal on their foreheads” — σφραγίς: the seal of chapter 7 protects God's servants. The demonic plague cannot touch those who belong to God.

scripture.text: They were given power, not to kill them, but to torment them for five months. Their torment was like the torment of a scorpion, when it strikes a person.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτούς, ἀλλ᾽ ἵνα βασανισθήσονται μῆνας πέντε, “They were given power, not to kill them, but to torment them for five months” — βασανίζω, to torture; μήν, from the time family: a month. Five months is the life cycle of a locust: a limited time. καὶ ὁ βασανισμὸς αὐτῶν ὡς βασανισμὸς σκορπίου, ὅταν παίσῃ ἄνθρωπον, “Their torment was like the torment of a scorpion, when it strikes a person” — βασανισμός, torment: painful, but not fatal.

scripture.text: In those days people will seek death, and will in no way find it. They will desire to die, and death will flee from them.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ζητήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν θάνατον καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρήσουσιν αὐτόν, “In those days people will seek death, and will in no way find it” — ἡμέρα, from the time family. οὐ μή, the strongest negative. καὶ ἐπιθυμήσουσιν ἀποθανεῖν, καὶ φεύγει ὁ θάνατος ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν, “They will desire to die, and death will flee from them” — the despair of a life without God: the torment they suffer is the inner anguish of those who have rejected Him.

scripture.text: The shapes of the locusts were like horses prepared for war. On their heads were something like golden crowns, and their faces were like people’s faces.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ τὰ ὁμοιώματα τῶν ἀκρίδων ὅμοια ἵπποις ἡτοιμασμένοις εἰς πόλεμον, “The shapes of the locusts were like horses prepared for war” — ὁμοίωμα, from the image family: a likeness, a form that resembles, as distinct from εἰκών, an image that represents. Joel said the locusts' appearance was like horses. καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν ὡς στέφανοι ὅμοιοι χρυσῷ, “On their heads were something like golden crowns” — στέφανος, from the crown family: they look like victors, but it is only a likeness. καὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὡς πρόσωπα ἀνθρώπων, “and their faces were like people’s faces” — intelligent, personal evil.

scripture.text: They had hair like women’s hair, and their teeth were like those of lions.
scripture.understanding: καὶ εἶχον τρίχας ὡς τρίχας γυναικῶν, “They had hair like women’s hair” — perhaps long and flowing, like the hair of the feared Parthian warriors. καὶ οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτῶν ὡς λεόντων ἦσαν, “and their teeth were like those of lions” — Joel described the locust army as having the teeth of a lion. A picture of terrible, devouring power.

scripture.text: They had breastplates, like breastplates of iron. The sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots, or of many horses rushing to war.
scripture.understanding: καὶ εἶχον θώρακας ὡς θώρακας σιδηροῦς, “They had breastplates, like breastplates of iron” — θώραξ: invulnerable to human resistance. καὶ ἡ φωνὴ τῶν πτερύγων αὐτῶν ὡς φωνὴ ἁρμάτων ἵππων πολλῶν τρεχόντων εἰς πόλεμον, “The sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots, or of many horses rushing to war” — Joel's words again: the noise of an invading army.

scripture.text: They have tails like those of scorpions, and stings. In their tails they have power to harm men for five months.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἔχουσιν οὐρὰς ὁμοίας σκορπίοις καὶ κέντρα, “They have tails like those of scorpions, and stings” — κέντρον, a sting, a goad. καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν ἀδικῆσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους μῆνας πέντε, “In their tails they have power to harm men for five months” — ἐξουσία, from the power family: their authority, given and limited; μήν, from the time family: five months, again.

scripture.text: They have over them as king the angel of the abyss. His name in Hebrew is “Abaddon”, but in Greek, he has the name “Apollyon”.
scripture.understanding: ἔχουσιν ἐπ᾽ αὐτῶν βασιλέα τὸν ἄγγελον τῆς ἀβύσσου, “They have over them as king the angel of the abyss” — Proverbs says ‘the locusts have no king’; these do. ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἀβαδδών, καὶ ἐν τῇ Ἑλληνικῇ ὄνομα ἔχει Ἀπολλύων, “His name in Hebrew is ‘Abaddon’, but in Greek, he has the name ‘Apollyon’” — both mean ‘Destroyer’. Some hear a jab at Domitian, who liked to be associated with the god Apollo. Satan's true character is destruction; Christ's is salvation.

scripture.text: The first woe is past. Behold, there are still two woes coming after this.
scripture.understanding: Ἡ οὐαὶ ἡ μία ἀπῆλθεν, “The first woe is past” — οὐαί. ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται ἔτι δύο οὐαὶ μετὰ ταῦτα, “Behold, there are still two woes coming after this” — the eagle's warning (8:13) is being fulfilled step by step.

scripture.text: The sixth angel sounded. I heard a voice from the horns of the golden altar which is before God,
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν, “The sixth angel sounded” — σαλπίζω: the second woe. καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μίαν ἐκ τῶν κεράτων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ χρυσοῦ τοῦ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ, “I heard a voice from the horns of the golden altar which is before God” — θυσιαστήριον: the altar where the saints' prayers were offered (8:3). The command comes from the place of prayer: this judgement too is an answer to the martyrs' cry.

scripture.text: saying to the sixth angel who had the trumpet, “Free the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates!”
scripture.understanding: λέγοντα τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀγγέλῳ, ὁ ἔχων τὴν σάλπιγγα, “saying to the sixth angel who had the trumpet” — σάλπιγξ. Λῦσον τοὺς τέσσαρας ἀγγέλους τοὺς δεδεμένους ἐπὶ τῷ ποταμῷ τῷ μεγάλῳ Εὐφράτῃ, “Free the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates!” — λύω, to loose; δέω, to bind. The Euphrates was the eastern border of the Roman Empire and of Israel's promised land; beyond it lay Parthia, Rome's feared enemy, and in the Old Testament the invading armies of Assyria and Babylon.

scripture.text: The four angels were freed who had been prepared for that hour and day and month and year, so that they might kill one third of mankind.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐλύθησαν οἱ τέσσαρες ἄγγελοι οἱ ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς τὴν ὥραν καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ μῆνα καὶ ἐνιαυτόν, “The four angels were freed who had been prepared for that hour and day and month and year” — four members of the time family in one phrase, joined by a single Greek article: ὥρα, the appointed hour; ἡμέρα, day; μήν, month; ἐνιαυτός, year. Not four periods added together, but one exact moment fixed by God down to the hour. ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, “so that they might kill one third of mankind” — τρίτος: now human life itself is struck.

scripture.text: The number of the armies of the horsemen was two hundred million. I heard the number of them.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν στρατευμάτων τοῦ ἱππικοῦ δισμυριάδες μυριάδων, “The number of the armies of the horsemen was two hundred million” — literally ‘twice ten thousand times ten thousand’: an unimaginable, uncountable host, a mirror image of the countless angels around the throne (5:11). ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν αὐτῶν, “I heard the number of them” — ἀκούω: as with the 144,000 (7:4), John hears a number.

scripture.text: Thus I saw the horses in the vision, and those who sat on them, having breastplates of fiery red, hyacinth blue, and sulfur yellow; and the horses’ heads resembled lions’ heads. Out of their mouths proceed fire, smoke, and sulfur.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ οὕτως εἶδον τοὺς ἵππους ἐν τῇ ὁράσει, “Thus I saw the horses in the vision” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family); ὅρασις, a vision. καὶ τοὺς καθημένους ἐπ᾽ αὐτῶν, ἔχοντας θώρακας πυρίνους καὶ ὑακινθίνους καὶ θειώδεις, “and those who sat on them, having breastplates of fiery red, hyacinth blue, and sulfur yellow” — the colours of the fire, smoke and sulfur that come from the horses' mouths. καὶ αἱ κεφαλαὶ τῶν ἵππων ὡς κεφαλαὶ λεόντων, “and the horses’ heads resembled lions’ heads” — καὶ ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν ἐκπορεύεται πῦρ καὶ καπνὸς καὶ θεῖον, “Out of their mouths proceed fire, smoke, and sulfur” — θεῖον, brimstone: the judgement of Sodom, and of the lake of fire (19:20).

scripture.text: By these three plagues were one third of mankind killed: by the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur, which proceeded out of their mouths.
scripture.understanding: ἀπὸ τῶν τριῶν πληγῶν τούτων ἀπεκτάνθησαν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, “By these three plagues were one third of mankind killed” — πληγή, a blow, a plague: from πλήσσω (8:12). ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ τοῦ καπνοῦ καὶ τοῦ θείου τοῦ ἐκπορευομένου ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν, “by the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur, which proceeded out of their mouths” — what comes from their mouths kills; what comes from Christ's mouth is the sword of truth (1:16).

scripture.text: For the power of the horses is in their mouths, and in their tails. For their tails are like serpents, and have heads, and with them they harm.
scripture.understanding: ἡ γὰρ ἐξουσία τῶν ἵππων ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν ἐστιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν, “For the power of the horses is in their mouths, and in their tails” — ἐξουσία, from the power family: delegated authority, once more. αἱ γὰρ οὐραὶ αὐτῶν ὅμοιαι ὄφεσιν, ἔχουσαι κεφαλάς, “For their tails are like serpents, and have heads” — ὄφις, a serpent: the sign of the ancient serpent, the devil (12:9). καὶ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀδικοῦσιν, “and with them they harm.”

scripture.text: The rest of mankind, who were not killed with these plagues, didn’t repent of the works of their hands, that they wouldn’t worship demons, and the idols of gold, and of silver, and of brass, and of stone, and of wood; which can’t see, hear, or walk.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, οἳ οὐκ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν ταῖς πληγαῖς ταύταις, “The rest of mankind, who were not killed with these plagues” — πληγή. οὐδὲ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν, “didn’t repent of the works of their hands” — μετανοέω; ἔργον, from the work family: the idols they made. ἵνα μὴ προσκυνήσουσιν τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ τὰ εἴδωλα, “that they wouldn’t worship demons, and the idols” — δαιμόνιον and εἴδωλον: behind the idols stand demons (1 Corinthians 10:20). ἃ οὔτε βλέπειν δύνανται οὔτε ἀκούειν οὔτε περιπατεῖν, “which can’t see, hear, or walk” — βλέπω, from the see family; δύναμαι, from the power family: idols have no ability at all — the Psalms' mockery of idols. People worship what is less than themselves.

scripture.text: They didn’t repent of their murders, their sorceries, their sexual immorality, or their thefts.
scripture.understanding: καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν φόνων αὐτῶν, “They didn’t repent of their murders” — μετανοέω, a second time: the tragic refrain. οὔτε ἐκ τῶν φαρμάκων αὐτῶν, “their sorceries” — φαρμακεία, the use of drugs and potions in magic and the occult. οὔτε ἐκ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῶν κλεμμάτων αὐτῶν, “their sexual immorality, or their thefts” — πορνεία, κλέμμα. Idolatry (v. 20) leads to the breaking of every commandment toward one's neighbour (v. 21). Judgement alone does not change hearts.

visualMeditations.title: The Pit Opened
visualMeditations.image: Picture a fallen star crashing to earth, handed a key by an unseen hand. He unlocks a shaft that goes down forever. Black smoke pours out like a furnace, blotting out the sun — and out of the smoke swarm creatures like locusts, millions of them.
visualMeditations.meaning: “The key to the pit of the abyss was given to him” (v. 1). Even the powers of hell act only when they are ‘given’ leave. The darkness is real and terrible, but it is on a leash.

visualMeditations.title: The Sealed Are Safe
visualMeditations.image: Picture the locust swarm descending on a city. They pass over fields and trees, and they swarm over the people — but every time they come near someone with God's seal on their forehead, they turn away as if from fire.
visualMeditations.meaning: “They were told that they should not hurt the grass of the earth... but only those people who don’t have God’s seal on their foreheads” (v. 4). Those who belong to God are not untouched by the troubles of the world, but they are protected from the demonic torment that falls on those without Him.

visualMeditations.title: Seeking Death
visualMeditations.image: Picture people in agony, not dying, longing for death as an escape — but death runs from them. Their pain is not only in their bodies but in their souls: lives empty of God, filled with torment.
visualMeditations.meaning: “In those days people will seek death, and will in no way find it. They will desire to die, and death will flee from them” (v. 6). A life cut off from God is a kind of torment that no escape can end. Only turning to Him brings rest.

visualMeditations.title: They Did Not Repent
visualMeditations.image: Picture the survivors of the plagues walking back into their temples, bowing again before golden statues that cannot see, hear or walk — and then going out to cheat, steal, sleep around and kill, as if nothing had happened.
visualMeditations.meaning: “The rest of mankind, who were not killed with these plagues, didn’t repent of the works of their hands” (v. 20). “They didn’t repent of their murders, their sorceries, their sexual immorality, or their thefts” (v. 21). Suffering alone does not change hearts. Only grace does.

structure.label: The Fifth Trumpet: Locusts from the Abyss (v. 1-12)
structure.body: A fallen star is given the key to the abyss and opens it; smoke darkens the sun, and locusts come out with power like scorpions to torment, not kill, those without God's seal for five months; people seek death and cannot find it; the locusts look like war horses with crowns, human faces, women's hair, lions' teeth and iron breastplates; their king is the angel of the abyss, Abaddon or Apollyon; the first woe is past.

structure.label: The Sixth Trumpet: Horsemen from the Euphrates (v. 13-19)
structure.body: A voice from the golden altar orders the release of four angels bound at the Euphrates, prepared for the exact hour, to kill a third of mankind; a cavalry of two hundred million appears, with breastplates of fire, hyacinth and sulfur, and horses with lions' heads breathing fire, smoke and sulfur, and tails like serpents.

structure.label: No Repentance (v. 20-21)
structure.body: The rest of mankind, who were not killed, still did not repent of worshipping demons and lifeless idols, nor of their murders, sorceries, sexual immorality or thefts.

sections.heading: Locusts from the Abyss
paragraphs: The fifth trumpet is the first of the three woes, and it moves from the natural world to the demonic. A star that has fallen from heaven is given “The key to the pit of the abyss” (v. 1). This is probably a fallen angel, perhaps Satan himself. He opens the abyss, the prison of evil spirits, and out of the smoke come locusts with the power of scorpions (vv. 2–3).

These are no ordinary locusts. They do not eat grass or trees (v. 4); they have human faces, women's hair, lions' teeth and iron breastplates (vv. 7–9); and they have a king, “the angel of the abyss” (v. 11). The prophet Joel had described a locust plague as an invading army; John describes a demonic army in the form of locusts. Their purpose is to torment people, not to kill them, “for five months” (v. 5).

Notice the limits. The key is ‘given’ to the fallen star (v. 1); power is ‘given’ to the locusts (v. 3); they may not harm vegetation, and above all they may not harm “those people who... have God’s seal on their foreheads” (v. 4). Their time is limited. Evil is real and terrible, but it is restrained by God, and it cannot destroy His people.

sections.heading: The Destroyer
paragraphs: The locusts' king is named in two languages: “His name in Hebrew is ‘Abaddon’, but in Greek, he has the name ‘Apollyon’” (v. 11). Both mean ‘Destroyer’. This is the true nature of the powers of darkness: they destroy. The devil comes, as Jesus said, only to steal, kill and destroy; Christ came that we might have life.

The torment the locusts bring is so terrible that “people will seek death, and will in no way find it” (v. 6). Many readers see in this a picture of the inner anguish of life without God: despair, addiction, fear, emptiness — the spiritual torment that sin and demonic deception bring. People seek escape but cannot find it.

Yet believers are protected. The seal of God is stronger than the sting of the scorpion. Paul says the Spirit warns that “in later times some will fall away from the faith, paying attention to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons” (1 Timothy 4:1); those sealed by God are kept from that destruction.

sections.heading: The Army from the Euphrates
paragraphs: The sixth trumpet sounds, and a voice comes “from the horns of the golden altar which is before God” (v. 13) — the altar of the saints' prayers. Four angels bound at the Euphrates are released, “prepared for that hour and day and month and year” (v. 15). God's timing is exact, down to the hour. Their task is to kill a third of mankind — the first time in the trumpets that human life is directly struck.

An enormous cavalry appears: “two hundred million” (v. 16). The horses have lions' heads and breathe fire, smoke and sulfur, and their tails are like serpents (vv. 17–19). For John's readers, the Euphrates suggested the Parthian cavalry that threatened Rome's eastern border, and before that the armies of Assyria and Babylon that God used to judge Israel. Some read this as a literal end-time army; others as demonic forces behind all the great wars of history. Either way it is a picture of overwhelming, devouring judgement.

Again the details point to the source: fire and sulfur (the judgement of Sodom and of the lake of fire), serpents (the ancient serpent, 12:9). The powers that serve evil end up destroying the very people who serve them.

sections.heading: Yet They Did Not Repent
paragraphs: The chapter ends with the saddest words in the trumpets: “The rest of mankind, who were not killed with these plagues, didn’t repent of the works of their hands, that they wouldn’t worship demons, and the idols of gold, and of silver, and of brass, and of stone, and of wood; which can’t see, hear, or walk” (v. 20). Like Pharaoh, they hardened their hearts.

The problem is first worship. Behind every idol stand demons (1 Corinthians 10:20). People bow to things that cannot see, hear or walk — things they made with their own hands — rather than to the living God who made them. And wrong worship always leads to wrong living: “They didn’t repent of their murders, their sorceries, their sexual immorality, or their thefts” (v. 21). The first commandments broken lead to the breaking of the rest.

This shows the purpose of the trumpets. They are judgements, but they are also calls to repentance, like the plagues of Egypt. That people do not repent shows that judgement alone cannot change the human heart. Only the grace of God, the testimony of His witnesses and the blood of the Lamb can do that — which is why chapters 10–11 turn to the message of God and His witnesses. Jesus said, “I tell you, no, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way” (Luke 13:3).

ntConnection.heading: The Abyss, the Destroyer and the Call to Repent
paragraphs: The demons Jesus cast out from the man of the Gerasenes “begged him that he would not command them to go into the abyss” (Luke 8:31). Other demons cried, “What do we have to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?” (Matthew 8:29). The demons know the abyss is their prison, and that their time is limited.

Jesus said, “I saw Satan having fallen like lightning from heaven” (Luke 10:18) — the fallen star of verse 1. Paul warns that “even Satan masquerades as an angel of light” (2 Corinthians 11:14) — like locusts with golden crowns and human faces, evil often looks glorious.

The list of sins in verse 21 matches Paul's list of the deeds of the flesh: “idolatry, sorcery, hatred, strife, jealousies, outbursts of anger, rivalries, divisions, heresies, envy, murders, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these” (Galatians 5:20–21). Paul warned that those who practise them will not inherit God's kingdom — and offered the way out: the fruit of the Spirit in those who belong to Christ.

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “depthless, i.e. (specially) (infernal) "abyss".” ἄβυσσος, from a- (not) and βυθός (depth), is the bottomless deep — in the Old Testament the watery deep of creation; in the New the prison of demons (Luke 8:31). In Revelation the locusts come out of it (9:2), the beast rises from it (11:7; 17:8), and in the end Satan is thrown into it and locked in (20:1–3). The key is always held by another: the abyss is a prison, not a throne.

Strong's: “a destroyer (i.e. Satan).” Ἀπολλύων, from ἀπόλλυμι (to destroy), is the Greek name of the angel of the abyss; Ἀβαδδών, from the Hebrew word for destruction, is his Hebrew name. Both describe what he does. The contrast with the Lamb could not be sharper: the Destroyer brings torment and death; the Lamb, who was slain, brings life. The devil's name tells you his purpose.

Strong's: “a locust (as pointed, or as lighting on the top of vegetation).” ἀκρίς is the ordinary locust — John the Baptist ate them. A locust swarm could strip a whole region bare; it was the eighth plague of Egypt and the subject of Joel's prophecy. Revelation's locusts are demonic: they have a king, human faces, crowns, and the sting of scorpions. They are a picture of evil spirits unleashed on a world that has rejected God.

Strong's: “to torture.” βασανίζω comes from βάσανος, a touchstone used to test metals, and then the torture used to test a witness. The locusts torment but do not kill (9:5). In 14:10 and 20:10 the word is used of the final punishment of the beast's worshippers and of the devil. Strikingly, in 11:10 the two prophets ‘tormented’ the earth-dwellers — by their testimony. The truth itself is torment to those who refuse it.

Strong's: “medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively).” φαρμακεία, from φάρμακον (a drug), is the use of drugs, potions and spells in magic and the occult. Our word ‘pharmacy’ comes from it. In the ancient world drugs, magic and idol worship were closely linked. Babylon ‘deceived all the nations’ by her φαρμακεία (18:23). Paul lists it among the deeds of the flesh (Galatians 5:20). It stands for every attempt to gain spiritual power apart from God.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit pulls back the curtain on the spiritual forces at work in the world — and on the human heart.

items.title: Evil Is on a Leash
items.body: The key to the abyss is ‘given’; the locusts' power is ‘given’; their time is limited to five months (vv. 1, 3, 5). The Spirit wants you to know that however dark things become, Satan acts only within limits God sets. You do not need to fear the Destroyer.

items.title: God's Seal Protects You
items.body: The locusts could harm only “those people who don’t have God’s seal on their foreheads” (v. 4). If you belong to Christ, you are sealed by His Spirit. The Spirit invites you to stand firm against fear, deception and spiritual attack, knowing you are His.

items.title: Don't Harden Your Heart
items.body: Even after terrible judgements, people “didn’t repent” (vv. 20–21). The Spirit asks gently: is there an area where God has been warning you, and you have not turned? Do not wait for the next trumpet. Repent today, while your heart is soft.

audit.title: The Idol Check
audit.body: What ‘works of your hands’ — achievements, possessions, technology, appearance — do you trust or serve in place of God (v. 20)?

audit.title: The Occult Check
audit.body: Have you ever sought spiritual power, guidance or healing through horoscopes, fortune-telling, charms or other practices outside God (v. 21)? Have you renounced them?

audit.title: The Repentance Check
audit.body: When hardship comes, does it soften your heart toward God or harden it (v. 20)?

practices.title: Clean House
practices.body: This week, walk through your home and your phone. Remove anything connected with the occult, idolatry or sexual immorality (v. 21). As you do, pray aloud: ‘I belong to the living God. I renounce every other power.’

practices.title: Pray for the Hardened
practices.body: Think of someone who has gone through great suffering yet still refuses God. Pray for them daily this week, asking that God would soften their heart and send someone to show them the Lamb's love.

prayerReflection: “Lord God Almighty, You hold the key to the abyss, and no evil power moves without Your permission. Thank You that the Destroyer cannot destroy those who bear Your seal. Thank You that I am sealed by Your Spirit as Your own. Protect me and my family from every deception, every torment and every spiritual attack. Where darkness has risen like smoke in my life or my community, let Your light break through. Lord, I confess that my heart can be hard. Show me any idol I have made with my own hands — anything I trust or serve in Your place — and give me grace to turn from it. Keep me from every sin of murder in my heart, every occult practice, every immorality and every theft. Soften the hearts of those I love who do not yet repent. Let them see the Lamb who was slain for them, and turn and live. In Jesus' name, Amen.”

storyConnections.title: The Locust Plague of Egypt
storyConnections.summary: When Pharaoh still refused to let Israel go, Moses stretched out his staff and the Lord sent an east wind that brought locusts over all Egypt. They covered the face of the land so that it was dark, and ate every plant and every fruit the hail had left. Pharaoh hurriedly confessed his sin and begged Moses to pray — but as soon as the locusts were gone, he hardened his heart again. The locusts of Revelation 9 recall that plague, and the refusal to repent in verses 20–21 recalls Pharaoh's hard heart.

storyConnections.title: Joel's Locust Army
storyConnections.summary: The prophet Joel saw a locust plague so terrible he described it as an invading army: the land was like Eden before them and a desolate wilderness behind; they looked like horses and ran like war horses; they leaped with the noise of chariots; the sun and moon were darkened. Joel called it the day of the Lord and summoned the people to return to God with fasting, weeping and mourning — ‘Tear your heart and not your garments’ — because He is gracious and merciful. Revelation's locusts carry the same message: turn to God before it is too late.

storyConnections.title: The Legion and the Abyss
storyConnections.summary: In the country of the Gerasenes, Jesus met a man possessed by many demons, who lived naked among the tombs and could not be chained. When Jesus asked his name, he said, ‘Legion’. The demons “begged him that he would not command them to go into the abyss” (Luke 8:31), and Jesus allowed them to go into a herd of pigs, which rushed into the lake and drowned. The man was found sitting at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind. The powers of the abyss fear Jesus — and He sets their captives free.
